editionData.title: Pentagon quietly adds dozens to tally of troops wounded amid Iran war; Saudis have not ruled out developing nuclear weapons,...
editionData.description: Global headlines: Pentagon quietly adds dozens to tally of troops wounded amid Iran war (With the addition of 29 U.S. sailors and eight Marines, the total number of personnel wounded since the start of hostilities has risen to 861, a Pentagon database shows); Saudis have not ruled out developing nuclear weapons, U.S. intelligence assesses (The sobering outlook has compounded concerns from some U.S. lawmakers about President Donald Trump’s agreement to assist the kingdom with establishing a civilian nuclear program); and Pope Leo visits secular France as surge of converts jolts a flagging faith (TikTok-savvy Catholic priests and candlelight Masses ending with recruiters sharing QR codes are helping the unbaptized connect with their grandparents’ faith). Markets leaned higher, with 5 of 7 tracked indexes up; Nikkei 225 up 1.30% was the largest move. Benchmarks tracked: S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, Euronext 100 Index, and Public Joint-Stock Company Moscow Exchange MICEX-RTS plus 3 more indexes. Hacker News: Revealing the details of how OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face (When a swarm of 700 OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face in July, they left behind a public trail of evidence); A single function Jev-like wrapper for LLMs, including vision models (I was intrigued by Jev and the self-hostable projects appearing around it, such as OpenJev and SemIf . Reading about them introduced me ...); and Plan mode is dead (Earlier this year, I believed planning was going to become the most important part of building software with AI). Product Hunt features Fewer (The launcher that counts how often you pick up your phone), Lisen (Free Read Aloud with Cartesia Voices), and Psst (A shared shopping list that remembers what things cost).
editionData.author: Sony Mathew

headlines.title: Pentagon quietly adds dozens to tally of troops wounded amid Iran war

headlines.title: Legacy of flying tigers lives on
headlines.summary: For those living Flying Tigers — a group of volunteer US pilots who came to China as early as 1941 to help fight against the invading Japanese troops — traveling back to China for this year's events marking the 85th anniversary of their great deeds is demanding due to their advanced age.
